page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server allocates 16 physical cores with a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the ecs.r7.4xlarge consistently in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-focused tests, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1575.0 and a multi-core score of 9464.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 20751.25. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 849.57 GB/sec, which drops to 102.07 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write bandwidth of 59.04 GB/sec. The system handles database operations with a PassMark database score of 7565.93 and processes 15.46 million Redis SET operations per second.

A key tradeoff of this instance is the complete absence of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for heavy local disk I/O or hardware-accelerated machine learning. While it handles small-scale LLM inference adequately, processing 1281.58 tokens per second on a 135M model, its performance drops to a weak tier of 30.95 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model. Given its high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and moderate data processing tasks.
